note: When Rav Ashi wanted his slave Minyamin immersed, he handed him to Ravina and Rav Aḥa son of Rava, warning that he would hold them responsible. They put a bridle on his neck, loosened it at the moment of immersion and tightened it again at once; the Gemara explains this let the water reach him and kept him from declaring first that he was immersing to become a free man. As he lifted his head from the water they put a bucket of clay on it and told him: Go, take this to your master's house.
why: Shmuel has just said that to stop a slave from declaring his immersion is for freedom, the owner must hold him tightly in the water; this incident shows how that was done.

terms.meaning: Dipping in a ritual pool; a slave immersed for slavery joins a Jewish household as a slave, but if he immerses for freedom it makes him a free Jew.

note: When Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda came from the Land of Israel, he reported that Rabbi Zakkai once recited a baraita before Rabbi Yoḥanan: an Ammonite woman is fit, her son from an Ammonite man is unfit, and her daughter is fit, but only when both parents converted; her daughter from an Ammonite married to a Jewish woman is unfit. Rabbi Yoḥanan told him: Go out and teach it outside. He took the teaching apart line by line, showing which parts were obvious, and rejected the last line.
why: Rav Yosef has just supported Rabbi Yoḥanan's view that the daughter of an Ammonite convert and a Jewish woman may marry a priest; this report shows Rabbi Yoḥanan dismissing a baraita that says otherwise.

note: The daughters-in-law of Abdan rebelled against their husbands, and Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi sent two Sages to look into it. When some women said to the daughters-in-law, Look, your husbands are coming, they answered: Let them be your husbands. Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said: There is no greater refusal than this.
why: The Gemara is asking whether something other than a formal refusal can end a minor's marriage, even after full marriage; it brings this case, argues the women may only have been betrothed, and still rules with Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira.

terms.meaning: A girl married off as a minor by her mother or brother could leave the marriage by declaring she refuses her husband, without a divorce.
Jewish marriage had two stages: betrothal, which already binds the couple, and full marriage, when they begin living together.

note: In a time of Roman persecution, a question had to be sent to the Sages. Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei says it concerned a girl who, as a minor, married a man's maternal uncle, and then married that man's paternal brother, who died: could she now refuse her first marriage, undoing it, so that her co-wife could marry the man in levirate marriage? Those involved hired two men for four hundred dinars, who asked Rabbi Akiva in prison and Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira in Netzivin. Both forbade it.
why: The Gemara is identifying which Sages stand behind the mishna's rules on a minor who left one husband by divorce and another by refusal; Rav cited this episode, and Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei corrects which question was asked.

people.name: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei
people.about: The Sage who says what question was really asked

people.name: Rabbi Akiva

people.name: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira
people.about: A Sage in Netzivin, who also forbids it

terms.meaning: A girl married off as a minor could leave the marriage by declaring she refuses her husband, which undoes it.
